title: Feature panel menu: Cut, Restore and Delete to Trash
subtitle: Three picks: where the panel's menu sits and how a cut feature reads, the Delete confirm for a feature and a goal, and features and goals in Settings › Trash. Owner, approver and viewer shown in each.

decisions.name: The panel's menu and a cut feature
decisions.question: Where does the feature panel's Cut, Restore and Delete live, and how does a cut feature's panel read?
decisions.common: Every Simple page opens the same panel, so this shows on all of them. The menu holds Cut (or Restore for a cut feature) and Move to Trash. Cut asks first and names what depends on it. An approver who is not the decider sees the same words as Propose, and who decides; a viewer sees no menu. Cut and Restore have Undo.

proposals.name: ⋯ menu by the close
proposals.what: A ⋯ button sits left of the × on the panel's header. It opens a short menu: Cut from the roadmap (or Restore to the roadmap for a cut feature) and Move to Trash…. A cut feature's panel keeps its normal look, its status chip reads Cut, and a grey strip under the title says 'Cut Nov 2 by Liam Brooks' with a Restore button, so Restore is one click and never hidden.
proposals.plus: Small and familiar (Priorities' rows already use ⋯); Restore is visible without opening anything; the strip says who cut it and when.
proposals.cost: The ⋯ hides what it holds until clicked; the cut strip takes one more row of the header on a cut feature.

proposals.why: It is where the owner asked for it (the header), it costs one small icon, and the one action people need on a cut feature, Restore, sits in plain sight on the strip. It reads the same on every page that opens the panel and on a phone.

proposals.name: Status chip is the menu
proposals.what: The status chip under the title becomes a button ('Planned ▾'). Clicking it opens Cut from the roadmap and Move to Trash…; on a cut feature it reads 'Cut ▾' with Restore inside, and 'Cut Nov 2 by Liam Brooks' follows it on the same line.
proposals.plus: No new control on the header; the menu sits on the very thing it changes (the status).
proposals.cost: A status chip that is also a menu is easy to miss, and its ▾ shows only to who may change it; Restore is two clicks.

proposals.name: Named Actions button
proposals.what: A labelled 'Actions ▾' button left of the ×. A cut feature's whole header turns grey with the title muted and 'Cut Nov 2 by Liam Brooks' in the header line; Restore lives only in the Actions menu.
proposals.plus: The word says what is behind it; the grey header tells at a glance that the feature is cut.
proposals.cost: A wider button on every panel header for actions used rarely; Restore takes two clicks; the grey header can read as 'disabled'.

proposals.name: Links in the Status row
proposals.what: No new header control: the Details section's Status row (read-only today) gets Cut and Move to Trash as links beside the status; for a cut feature it reads 'Cut Nov 2 by Liam Brooks · Restore · Move to Trash'.
proposals.plus: Nothing added to the header; the actions sit beside the status they change, in words.
proposals.cost: It is not on the header the owner picked: the row is at the bottom of a long panel, below Dates, Goal, Links and Milestone, so it is found only by scrolling.

decisions.name: The Delete confirm
decisions.question: What does the Delete confirm say for a feature and for a goal, and how hard is it to press?
decisions.common: Delete always sends to Trash for 30 days; nothing is deleted for good. After it the feature leaves the roadmap and a toast offers Undo. Features that depended on it lose that link; decisions that name it stay. A goal's features stay on the roadmap under No goal. An approver who is not the decider proposes it.

proposals.name: One line, counts behind (i)
proposals.what: The confirm asks 'Move Alert rules engine to Trash?' with one short line of counts ('2 links, 3 decisions and a goal go with it.'); the (i) beside it lists them by name, floating beside the dialog. An (i) by Cancel says where Restore lives.
proposals.plus: Shortest confirm; nothing to read for a feature with no links.
proposals.cost: Who loses a link is hidden behind the (i), so the owner may trash a feature others depend on without seeing their names.

proposals.name: List what points at it
proposals.what: The confirm lists, one row each: Needed by (the features that lose the link, by name), Depends on, Decisions that name it (they stay), Milestone and Goal. An (i) by Cancel says 'Restore it from Settings › Trash for 30 days.' and 'Not now? Cut keeps it on the roadmap.' A goal's confirm lists the features that stay under No goal and its measure.
proposals.plus: Everything at stake in one look; the Cut hint steers 'not now' away from Delete.
proposals.cost: A taller dialog (five rows) even for a feature with nothing linked; a goal with many features shortens its list to four names and a count.

proposals.why: The owner sees by name what the delete touches before pressing it, with no extra step; the same five rows read alike for every feature, and the (i) by Cancel says it can come back.

proposals.name: Type the name if needed
proposals.what: Like B, but when other features depend on it (or a goal still holds features) the Move to Trash button stays off until the name is typed.
proposals.plus: A hard stop exactly when a delete breaks others' links.
proposals.cost: An extra step for an action Restore can undo anyway; typing long names is slow, worst on a phone.

proposals.name: No confirm, Undo
proposals.what: Move to Trash acts at once: the panel closes, the feature leaves the roadmap and a toast says 'Moved Alert rules engine to Trash' with Undo.
proposals.plus: Fastest; nothing to dismiss; Restore and Undo make it safe.
proposals.cost: One slip removes a feature others depend on; after the toast is gone it is back only from Settings › Trash, where only an owner restores; an approver proposes it.

decisions.name: Settings › Trash
decisions.question: How does Settings › Trash list features and goals beside documents?
decisions.common: Each row says who deleted it and when, days left, and Restore; an (i) says what Restore puts back: a feature's dates, links, milestone and goal ('Milestone: None' when it had none), a goal's measure and its features' links. Owners restore; approvers propose a restore of a feature or goal; viewers read; documents stay owners only.

proposals.name: One list, kind chip
proposals.what: One Deleted list, newest first, each row led by a kind chip (Feature, Goal, PRD, Update…), its roadmap in grey, who deleted it and when, days left, an (i) with what Restore puts back, and Restore.
proposals.plus: Today's page, with one chip added; the thing just deleted is always on top.
proposals.cost: With many deletes of one kind the others are pushed down; no way to see only goals.

proposals.why: Trash is a short list people visit to find one thing they just deleted; newest first with a chip finds it fastest, and it keeps today's page as it is.

proposals.name: Grouped by kind
proposals.what: Three panels: Features, Goals, Documents, each with its count and its own rows newest first.
proposals.plus: Each kind in its own place; counts at a glance.
proposals.cost: Long Features panel pushes Goals and Documents below the fold; a goal deleted today sits under weeks-old features.

proposals.name: Filtered tabs
proposals.what: Tabs above the list: All, Features, Goals, Documents with counts; All is one list with kind chips like A.
proposals.plus: One list by default, and one click narrows it.
proposals.cost: One more control on a page with little in it; a tab left on Goals hides the feature someone is looking for.
